eval.adviseWrong2: Buy the strongest product we have, just in case.
eval.n.emergency: This customer needed emergency services. Dispensing a product delayed urgent care.
eval.n.referral: This customer needed to be referred to a doctor — the symptoms are not suitable for self-care.
eval.n.askSymptoms: Asking about other symptoms would have revealed the red flags.
eval.n.better: Acceptable, but a more suitable option was available.
eval.n.advice: This situation called for advice rather than an additional medicine.
eval.n.wrongProduct: The selected product does not address the customer’s problem.
eval.n.budget: The total ({total}) was well above the customer’s budget ({budget}). Consider a generic option.
eval.n.generic: Good value: you offered a cost-saving generic.
eval.n.alt: You offered an alternative with the same active ingredient — great when a brand is out of stock.
eval.n.underTriaged: Correct to refer, but these symptoms needed EMERGENCY services, not a routine doctor visit.
eval.n.referralNo: Referral was safe, but this problem was suitable for pharmacist-led care with an OTC option or advice.
eval.n.emergencyMinor: Calling emergency services for a minor problem diverts urgent resources.
eval.n.needReferral: This customer needed referral, not self-care advice.
eval.n.otcAvailable: A suitable OTC product was available for this customer.
eval.n.badCounsel: The explanation you gave contained inaccurate or unsafe information.

w.cert.title: PHARMACY CERTIFIED
gd.intro.consult: Follow these steps in order. Steps marked ★ are the important questions for this case.
gd.intro.level: Complete these objectives to finish the level. Tap “Take me there” and your pharmacist walks there.
gd.intro.pos: The customer is waiting at the cash counter.
gd.intro.event: Something in the pharmacy needs your attention.
gd.intro.insp: Answer every question correctly. Study modules in the training library help.
gd.intro.wait: A customer is on the way. Stand at the counter and wait for them.
gd.readRx: Tap “Prescription” and check the name, date, medicine and signature.
gd.askMore: Optional: ask the other questions for more detail.
gd.decide.dispense: Decision: this customer can be helped with a medicine — {label}.
gd.decide.doctor: Decision: do NOT give medicine. Refer the customer to a doctor.
gd.decide.emergency: Decision: RED FLAGS — this is an emergency. Call emergency services.
gd.decide.advise: Decision: no medicine is needed. Give self-care advice.
gd.decide.hidden: Decide what to do (unlocks after the ★ questions).
gd.find: Open the medicine cabinet and search “{q}”. Pick a product marked ★.
gd.read: Tap the product, read the MEDICINE INFORMATION, then tap ADD TO CUSTOMER.
gd.safety: Tap “Safety check”. If everything is green, tap Dispense.
gd.explain: Choose the correct explanation for the customer (use “Mentor tip” if unsure).
gd.payment: Walk to the POS (cash counter) and take payment.
gd.adviseStep: Tap “Advise only” and choose the safe self-care advice.
gd.why.consult: Asking the right questions reveals allergies, other medicines and red flags. Safety always comes before selling.
gd.goPOS: Walk to the POS (cash counter) behind the counter.
gd.choosePay: Choose UPI, Card or Cash, then tap “Complete payment”.
gd.openEvent: Open the alert and choose the safe action.
gd.eventTip: Tip: the safe answer protects patients — record, quarantine and fix the cause.
gd.inspWrong: One wrong answer restarts the inspection from question 1.
gd.waitCust: Wait for the customer to arrive, then tap them to talk.
gd.careerServe: Talk to customers at the counter and follow the consultation steps.
gd.careerInsp: Surprise inspections can happen at any time — keep studying.
gd.obj.inspectShelf: Walk to any medicine shelf and tap it to look at the products.
gd.obj.viewDetails: Open the medicine cabinet, tap a medicine and tap VIEW DETAILS ({n} needed).
gd.obj.search: Open the cabinet and search a symptom, for example “fever”.
gd.obj.serve: Serve customers: talk to them at the counter, ask questions, then dispense, refer or advise.
gd.obj.event: Wait for the alert, then handle it safely.
gd.obj.restock: Go to the POS → Stock orders and reorder a low section.
gd.obj.modules: Open the training library and study {n} modules.
gd.obj.practice: Open the training library and score {n}/10 or more in the practice quiz.
gd.n.dispense: Give {label}. Open the cabinet and search “{q}”.
gd.n.trayGood: Good choice! Now tap “Safety check”, then Dispense.
gd.n.trayBad: {name} is not right for this customer. Remove it and look for {label}.
gd.n.doctor: This needs a doctor. Tap “Refer customer” → “Refer to a doctor”.
gd.n.emergency: RED FLAGS! Tap “Refer customer” → “Call emergency services”.
gd.n.advise: No medicine is needed. Tap “Advise only” and give self-care advice.
gd.h.askFirst: First ask the ★ key questions — the answers decide which medicine is safe.
gd.h.dispense: Look for {label}. Products marked ★ are safe matches for this customer.
gd.h.noMed: This customer should not get a medicine — {what}.
gd.v.good: Good match for this customer. Read the details, then tap ADD TO CUSTOMER.
gd.v.ok: Acceptable, but {label} is a better choice.
gd.v.wrong: This does not treat the customer’s problem. Look for {label}.
gd.v.unknown: Careful — you have not asked about {q}. This product may not be safe.
gd.v.refer: This customer needs referral, not a medicine.
gd.v.advise: No medicine is needed for this customer.
gd.v.askFirst: Ask the ★ key questions before choosing a medicine.
gd.v.rx: Prescription-only: check it matches the prescription exactly.
gd.s.empty: Add a product to the tray first (or refer / advise).
gd.s.unasked: You have not asked: {list}. Go back and ask before dispensing.
gd.s.advise: No medicine is needed — go back and tap “Advise only”.
gd.s.change: Not the best product. Tap “Change products” and look for {label}.
gd.r.emergency: Correct — these are red flags. Choose “Call emergency services”.
gd.r.dispense: a suitable medicine can be given
